ledger.claim: The driver's own trace places him inside the pickup geofence for a continuous run of only 434 seconds, and the free waiting period in force for this STANDARD-zone trip is 180 seconds — but the trip record shows the driver cancelled at 22:13:25, which is 434 seconds after the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 22:06:11. On its face the dwell clears the 180-second minimum, so the rider cannot win on POL-NS-06 shortfall alone; the rider's case must rest on the arrival-marker and reason-code limbs instead.

The trip record's own event log shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 22:06:11 and the free waiting period of 180 seconds started at 22:06:13, yet the driver did not cancel until 22:13:25 — a wait of 7 minutes 12 seconds. The rider was charged $4.50 for a no-show the driver's own telemetry shows was not a no-show at all: the driver simply gave up after waiting far longer than the 3-minute free period, and the rider's device was stationary at a single location throughout the window, consistent with a rider waiting at the pin.

The rider's track shows 70 fixes, all at zero speed, with a mean distance of 870.57 m from the pickup pin and a minimum distance of 866.56 m — the rider never came within the 100 m rider-presence radius for STANDARD zone. This is the rider's own device placing them roughly 870 m from the pickup point for the entire window, which affirmatively fails POL-NS-04 limb (c) and means the rider was not at the pin. The rider's claim that the driver 'cancelled on me again' is not supported by the rider's own GPS.

The driver's profile shows 3 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days against 40 completed trips — a rate of 0.075, which is below the 0.08 threshold in POL-NS-07's anti-farming check. The anti-farming check therefore does NOT trip, and the driver is entitled to compensation at 80% of the $4.50 cancellation fee, i.e. $3.60, with the fee standing as charged. The rider's $4.50 charge is not refundable on this record.

The rider's profile shows zero no-show disputes in the trailing 30 days and zero disputes with this counterparty in the trailing 90 days, so neither POL-NS-09(c) nor POL-NS-09(d) is engaged. There is no pattern of abuse on either side that would require escalation, and the case is decidable on the evidence as it stands.

The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02752-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 — no advisory covers Blk 640 Jurong West St 61 in this window. Under POL-NS-06(i) a MISSING traffic_advisory makes limb (i) unavailable, so the driver cannot accumulate dwell across separate in-geofence intervals. However, the trace shows only one in-geofence interval (run_count = 1), so limb (i) is not needed here and its unavailability does not change the outcome.

ledger.claim: The chat log shows a single message from the driver at 22:06:31 saying 'im at the pickup point', read by the rider at 22:07:01. The rider sent no reply and no locating or coordinating message during the waiting window. POL-NS-04 limb (a) requires the rider to have sent at least one locating or coordinating message; the rider sent none, so POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider regardless of limb (c).

The fare breakdown shows the cancellation fee line at $4.50, which reconciles with the platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of $4.50 in the trip record. There is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect: the charged amount matches the net figure produced by the resolution rule, so the fare evidence is clean and the charge is properly recorded.

The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 22:06:11 and a wait timer started at 22:06:13, and the driver terminated the trip at 22:13:25 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event anywhere in the record. Limb (a) and limb (d) of the baseline chargeable no-show are therefore both satisfied on the platform's own telemetry.

The driver's own trace places him inside the STANDARD arrival radius for a single continuous qualifying run of 434 seconds, from 22:06:11 to 22:13:25, across 44 qualifying fixes. That is well past the 180 second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180), so limb (c) of POL-NS-01 is satisfied on the measured dwell and not merely on the arrival tap.

The arrival marker is not false. The trace shows the driver stationary at the pickup pin (min_distance_m 0.0) with a distinct speed of 0.0 kph during the dwell, and the arrival event timestamp 22:06:11 matches the first fix of the qualifying run exactly, so there is no distance-over-300 m and no speed-at-or-above-15 kph trigger under POL-NS-05. The waiting clock runs from the true in-geofence entry, and it still clears the minimum.

There is no waiting-period shortfall to refund. The effective in-geofence dwell of 434 seconds exceeds the 180 second minimum by 254 seconds (derived shortfall_sec = -254.0), so POL-NS-06 does not bite. Limb (i) of POL-NS-06 is unavailable in any event: EV-ADVIS-02752-01 is MISSING, and a MISSING traffic_advisory cannot be asserted to accumulate dwell or to excuse anything.

ledger.claim: The rider was not at the pickup point. The rider's own track shows 70 fixes at a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph, with a minimum distance of 866.56 m and a mean of 870.57 m from the pin - far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider presence radius - and zero qualifying rider fixes inside it. The rider's device was stationary roughly 870 m away for the whole waiting window.

The driver did what the platform asks of a waiting driver: he sent one in-app message at 22:06:31 reading 'im at the pickup point', delivered at 22:06:32 and read by the rider at 22:07:01. The rider never replied and never placed an in-app call (trip_record.in_app_calls is empty). The driver then waited out the full period before cancelling at 22:13:25.

The rider cannot be exonerated under POL-NS-04. Limb (a) requires a rider message during the waiting window that is locating or coordinating; the chat log holds exactly one message and it is the driver's, not the rider's. Limb (c) is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes, since the rider's track sits about 870 m from the pin throughout. POL-NS-04 therefore does not apply and the dispute is decided under POL-NS-01.

The fee charged reconciles with the policy figure. The fare breakdown shows a cancellation_fee of 4.50 SGD against a platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.50, a difference of 0.00, so there is no integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d) and no basis to disturb the line.

The driver's payout is fixed by POL-NS-07 at 80 percent of the net cancellation fee in force: 3.60 SGD of the 4.50 SGD charged, the residual 0.90 SGD being the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 3, which is below the threshold of 4, and 3 divided by completed_trips_30d of 40 is 0.075, which is below the 0.08 rate limb. Both limbs are required and neither holds, so compensation is payable rather than withheld.

No escalation trigger is engaged. The two admissible artifacts agree rather than contradict on arrival and dwell, there is no same-rider-same-driver dispute history (both disputes_with_counterparty_90d fields are 0), rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and no deciding fact rests on an artifact impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d) - the trace has 100 percent coverage, no gaps, a 10 second cadence and both tracks present. The case is decidable on the record.

I concede the one point that does not help the driver: the driver's profile carries no_show_terminations_30d of 3 in the trailing 30 days, which is a real pattern worth watching. It does not reach the POL-NS-07 anti-farming threshold, which requires 4 or more AND a rate above 0.08, and it is not a ground for any adverse finding on this trip. I note it rather than argue it away.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your $4.50 no-show cancellation fee stands and is not refunded. To the driver: you are paid SGD 3.60, being 80% of the $4.50 fee under POL-NS-07. The record shows a valid no-show. Driver DRV-09752 accepted trip TRP-02752 at 21:57:46, and trip record EV-TRIP-02752 carries a driver 'arrived' event at 22:06:11 with the wait timer starting at 22:06:13. GPS trace EV-GPS-02752 places the driver inside the STANDARD 50 m arrival radius continuously from 22:06:11 to the 22:13:25 cancellation (44 qualifying fixes, a single 434-second run, minimum distance 0 m), so POL-NS-01 limb (b) holds, and the arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05 (the driver was stationary at the pin at 22:06:11, not more than 300 m away and not travelling at or above 15 km/h). The 434-second dwell exceeds the 180-second free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180 s; derived shortfall_sec = -254.0), so limb (c) holds; and the trip was terminated by the driver under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event at 22:13:25, after the dwell elapsed, so limb (d) holds. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold, so the $4.50 fee is chargeable. Your argument that this was not a real no-show because the driver simply gave up after waiting, and that your device was stationary, does not change that: your own rider track (in EV-GPS-02752) shows 70 fixes at 0.0 km/h with a minimum distance of 866.56 m and a mean of 870.57 m from the pickup pin — roughly 870 m away, far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, with zero qualifying in-radius fixes — so you were not at the pin during the waiting window. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate you: limb (a) needs a locating or coordinating message from the rider, and the only message in chat log EV-CHAT-02752 is the driver's at 22:06:31 ('im at the pickup point'), which you read at 22:07:01 and did not answer; limb (c) fails affirmatively on your own track. POL-NS-11 does not apply because your rider track is present. POL-NS-06 does not bite: there is no waiting-period shortfall (dwell exceeds the minimum by 254 seconds). The fee line reconciles — fare breakdown EV-FARE-02752 charges $4.50 against platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of $4.50, difference 0.00 — so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect, and the trace and chat show no clock skew, trace gap or truncated log under POL-NS-08(a) to (c). No artifact carrying a deciding fact is impaired (all deciding artifacts weigh 1.0), so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. POL-NS-07 fixes your payout, driver, at 80% of the net fee: 0.8 x $4.50 = $3.60, the residual $0.90 being the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 3 (below the 4-or-more limb) and 3 / 40 completed trips = 0.075 (at or below the 0.08 rate limb); both limbs are required, so compensation is paid rather than withheld. No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is engaged — the admissible artifacts agree rather than contradict, both disputes_with_counterparty_90d fields are 0, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and no deciding fact rests on evidence impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d). Under POL-GEN-03 the ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and amount_sgd carries the same $3.60; the rider's charge is not refunded. No clause produces a referral (the arrival marker is not false, so POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire). The monetary effect (SGD 3.60) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically under POL-GEN-05.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
